name: Rudram-II Anti-Radiation Missile

what_it_is.prose: Rudram-II is India's indigenous anti-radiation missile designed by the Research Centre Imarat (RCI) of DRDO for the Suppression/Destruction of Enemy Air Defences (SEAD/DEAD) role. The missile uses passive radar homing (home-on-radiation) to detect and track enemy radar emissions, combined with INS/GPS for mid-course guidance, enabling it to autonomously seek and destroy radar installations, surface-to-air missile (SAM) sites, and other air defence systems. With an estimated range of ~100-150 km, the Rudram-II gives the Indian Air Force a dedicated indigenous SEAD/DEAD capability previously reliant on the Russian Kh-31P anti-radiation missile. The missile is primarily intended for launch from the Su-30MKI. The first test firing was reported in 2022, and the programme is in the tested/procurement phase. Rudram-II is part of a broader family of Rudram missiles (Rudram-I was an earlier development).

faq.question: What is an anti-radiation missile?
faq.answer: An anti-radiation missile (ARM) is designed to detect and home in on enemy radar and radio emissions. It is used in the SEAD/DEAD (Suppression/Destruction of Enemy Air Defences) role to destroy enemy radar installations, SAM sites, and air defence command systems, thereby creating corridors for follow-on strike aircraft.

faq.question: What is the difference between Rudram-I and Rudram-II?
faq.answer: Rudram-I was an earlier anti-radiation missile variant, while Rudram-II is the improved development with estimated range of ~100-150 km and enhanced seeker technology. Rudram-II is intended as the primary SEAD/DEAD missile for the Indian Air Force, replacing or supplementing the Russian Kh-31P.

faq.question: Which aircraft will carry Rudram-II?
faq.answer: Rudram-II is primarily designed for the Su-30MKI, with the first test firings conducted from that platform. Future integration is planned for the Tejas Mk-2 and potentially the AMCA (Advanced Medium Combat Aircraft).
